slot.brief: Magnetic flux through a stationary loop changes linearly with time (uniform field growing/shrinking); compute average induced emf and current through a resistance over a time interval.

stem: The magnetic flux through a single-turn stationary loop decreases uniformly from $12$ mWb to zero in $4$ s. If the loop resistance is $3\ \Omega$, what is the induced current?

verdicts.working: Induced emf = |ΔΦ|/Δt = 12 mWb / 4 s = 3 mV. Current = 3 mV / 3 Ω = 1 mA.

working:
$|\mathcal{E}|=\dfrac{|\Delta\Phi|}{\Delta t}=\dfrac{12\times10^{-3}}{4}=3\times10^{-3}$ V
$I=|\mathcal{E}|/R=\dfrac{3\times10^{-3}}{3}=1\times10^{-3}$ A $=1$ mA

Independent check: Induced emf = |ΔΦ|/Δt = 12 mWb / 4 s = 3 mV. Current = 3 mV / 3 Ω = 1 mA.
